A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R-LiViT dataset and benchmarks, with readable text, tables, and figures. All pages were inspected, including v3's added Appendix A; v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, an anonymization experiment, and LiDAR detection, tracking, and RGB-T detection results in Figures 6–7 and Tables 3–6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and dataset analyses and additionally reports a calibration reprojection error.

M1.justification: No revised model, training objective, or inference procedure is reported. The added homography description explains the existing thermal-to-RGB alignment; the detection, tracking, and late-fusion procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and testing retain the same three intersections, day/night conditions, modalities, and detection/tracking tasks. Seven LiDAR classes were already listed in v1 Section 3.2, so correcting the abstract from six to seven does not add coverage. New Table 1 datasets provide comparative context rather than additional model benchmarks.

E2.justification: Tables 3–6 retain the same evaluated methods: PointPillars, PointRCNN, PV-RCNN; AB3DMOT, SimpleTrack, Mahalanobis; and Faster R-CNN, YOLOv8, RT-DETR. Table 1 adds related datasets, not competing detection or tracking methods.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces the diversity descriptors with pedestrian density and scopes comparisons to publicly available dataset versions. Section 3.2 retains the 80/20 sequence-level split but drops the explicit consecutive-sequence grouping safeguard. This changes the reported evaluation description without establishing that data were repartitioned or experiments rerun.

E4.justification: Section 3.1 adds a limited alignment-quality diagnostic: mean reprojection error of 0.038. The anonymization experiment, modality/day-night comparisons, and annotation analyses remain unchanged. Appendix A supplies illustrative samples without a new ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions average experiments over three random seeds and report sample standard deviations for the anonymization results in Table 3. No uncertainty-estimation procedure, run count, or statistical testing practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 are numerically identical. v3 adds reprojection error 0.038 and Table 1 pedestrian densities, including 9.61 for R-LiViT and 27.56 for V2X-Real-I2I. It also changes independent scenarios from 151 to 150 and corrects intersection 2's day/night shares from 24%/34% to 34%/24%.

T1.justification: Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs. The added homography description and pedestrian-density explanation introduce no mathematical derivation or substantive formal change.

C1.justification: The main contribution remains a roadside LiDAR-RGB-thermal dataset emphasizing vulnerable road users, with aligned RGB-T annotations and detection/tracking benchmarks. Corrected summary counts do not redefine this contribution or its novelty claim.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning anonymization, sparse point clouds, difficult VRU tracking, and improved person recall through fusion are retained. Section 3.3 preserves the same limitations concerning synchronization, annotation consistency, cross-modal IDs, and camera coverage.

D1.justification: v3 replaces release-upon-acceptance placeholders with a dataset DOI and code repository links, explains homography estimation, and explicitly states use of the predefined training/test splits. Conversely, it removes details about data selection, repeated annotation-quality checks, and consecutive-sequence grouping. These are documentation changes, not demonstrated pipeline changes.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and Table 1 add DAIR-V2X-I, RCooper, and V2X-Real-I2I, with three corresponding references. This broadens the roadside/cooperative-perception comparison and contextualizes pedestrian density while preserving the paper's overall research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites parts of the roadside-dataset discussion, shortens several explanatory passages, corrects terminology, and updates an author affiliation. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact; the new appendix contains a short sample caption.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains three dataset rows and replaces its diversity column with pedestrian density. Appendix A adds Figure 8 with six cross-modal sample rows. Existing Figures 1–7 and evaluation-table designs are retained, with limited layout shifts.

improvement.justification: v3 improves accuracy and usability through corrected dataset counts and percentages, concrete data/code references, broader related-dataset comparisons, and clearer visual examples. Removing the consecutive-sequence split safeguard and quality-control details weakens reproducibility documentation, but does not establish changed experimental practice. With the benchmark evidence unchanged, the net improvement is limited.
